lines.text: Every Indian household knows the power cut. Almost nobody keeps a record, and the only log is usually the utility's.
BijliLog is a power-cut log for your PIN code, kept by neighbours, and stored on Arkiv instead of on our server.
Type a PIN code. This live cut is labelled demo data. It is a two-hour lease: each neighbour who taps Still dark renews it, and if nobody does, it expires on its own.
Neighbours are counted as distinct people, and every record links to the Arkiv explorer, so nobody has to trust us.
When power returns, the cut becomes a read-only record kept for a year. Here is the history for this PIN: cuts, hours without power, the longest cut, and night-time cuts.
Filter to cuts a neighbour confirmed, or cuts longer than four hours, then download a CSV for your complaint. Every row carries its Arkiv entity key.
The page reads Arkiv straight from your browser. These are the exact queries it runs, so you can reproduce them.
It works in Hindi too, because this is built for people across India.
Why Arkiv? Expiry gives each cut a lease. Permissionless extension lets any neighbour renew it. Atomic batches keep a confirmation and its renewal together. WebSocket events update the page live.
A testnet demo with synthetic data, no personal data stored. Open source under MIT, built with AI assistance.
